title: RATE decision event
description: Shape of a typed assessment/decision event for a coordination bridge. Harvested and generalized. This schema validates STRUCTURE ONLY. It cannot establish that a diagnosis is true, that a readiness count is correct, or that a bound digest is still current — those are algorithmic obligations enforced in code, not shape. See schemas/README.md. Role names, the pinned diagnosis vocabulary, and objective identifiers are project policy supplied by the deployment, not fixed here.

event.description: Discriminates this envelope from other bridge events.

writer.description: Emitting role. The value is topology policy; the field is required so authority is attributable.

objectives.description: Per-objective diagnosis. A single global diagnosis is refused: assessment is per objective.

rate.description: R: wrong problem. A: right problem, wrong approach. T: met, or provably won't be. E: on track.

diagnosis.description: A diagnosis MUST name a type and a falsifier. A bare enum tag with no way to be proven wrong is refused — a claim that cannot fail is not a diagnosis.

type.description: One value from the deployment's pinned diagnosis vocabulary. The vocabulary is project policy; validate closed-set membership in code or in a project overlay of this schema. Grounded examples from the source record: 'invalid_measure', 'delayed_effect'.

falsification_condition.description: A concrete, observable condition under which this diagnosis would be wrong.

diagnosis_truth.description: Whether the diagnosis is TRUE is undecidable by shape. It is always not_established here; an underdetermined case is routed to discrimination, never validated as truth.

waiver.description: Optional. A waiver is DATED, CITED, and EXPIRING. It may suppress a warning but never removes a contradicted-and-open row from the readiness count (that suppression is enforced in code, not here). An expired waiver must be refused by the reader.

disposition.description: A disposition binds the digest of the governing rubric/order it was judged against. When that digest changes the disposition is stale — freshness is enforced in code by comparing governing_digest to the current standard; this schema only requires the binding to be present.

governing_digest.description: sha256 of the rubric/order this disposition was judged against.

closure_evidence.description: References to the evidence that closes a contradicted row. A contradicted row whose disposition names no closure evidence is OPEN regardless of applicability or waiver.
